We further demonstrate that hybridisation of a short DNA strand to the target complex–away from the toehold domain–speeds up TMSD, hence providing a route for allosteric modulation of the reaction rate. Our results highlight the substantial effect of topological confinement on TMSD. These effects must be considered in the optimal design of dynamic nanostructures and molecular reaction networks while offering convenient strategies for the fine-tuning and modulation of reaction rates.
items.authors: Andrew Stannard, Aditya Sengar, Alexander H. Clowsley, Christian Soeller, Thomas E. Ouldridge, Lorenzo Di Michele
items.title_zh: 拓扑约束下的踏脚石介导链置换研究
items.summary_zh: 踏脚石介导链置换（TMSD）是合成核酸纳米系统动态驱动的最简单机制，广泛应用于生物传感、分子计算、数据存储与检索及合成生物学。本文研究了一种简单的生理相关配置，其中踏脚石域位于DNA“气泡”中，即两条链在此区域脱配。研究表明，这种拓扑约束使TMSD的速率降低了约1-3个数量级，原因在于TMSD自由能景观的变化。此外，短DNA链与目标复合物的杂交（远离踏脚石域）加速了TMSD，提供了反应速率的变构调节途径。结果强调了拓扑约束对TMSD的显著影响，这些影响在动态纳米结构和分子反应网络的优化设计中必须考虑，同时为精细调节和调控提供了便利策略。
items.l1_lead: 研究表明，拓扑约束显著降低踏脚石介导链置换的速率，并提供了调节反应速率的新策略，强调了其在动态纳米结构设计中的重要性。
items.l2_summary: 踏脚石介导链置换（TMSD）是合成核酸纳米系统中一种重要的动态驱动机制，广泛应用于生物传感、分子计算、数据存储与检索及合成生物学。本文探讨了一种生理相关的配置，其中踏脚石域位于DNA“气泡”中，即两条链在该区域脱配。研究发现，这种拓扑约束显著降低了TMSD的速率，约降低了1-3个数量级，主要原因在于TMSD自由能景观的变化。此外，短DNA链与目标复合物的杂交（远离踏脚石域）能够加速TMSD反应，提供了一种反应速率的变构调节途径。这些结果强调了拓扑约束对TMSD的显著影响，表明在动态纳米结构和分子反应网络的优化设计中，必须考虑这些影响。同时，这项研究为精细调节和调控提供了便利的策略，推动了相关领域的发展。

items.title: Eugenol Sustained Release from a Non-Innocent Zn-MOF for Antimicrobial Fruit Preservation
items.abstract: Active packaging is an effective strategy to extend food shelf life and reduce waste. In this work, a Zn-based Metal-Organic Framework (ZnBDP) was loaded with the natural antimicrobial eugenol using a vapour-phase impregnation, achieving complete encapsulation within the MOF pores (21 wt%), enabling sustained release in water over 3.5 months. Considering the bioactivity of Zn2+ and eugenol, the combined bactericidal and fungicidal effect of eugenol@ZnBDP_V was enhanced. Eugenol@ZnBDP_V demonstrated a superior activity against the bacteria Escherichia coli compared to free eugenol or pristine ZnBDP. 3 Further, important antifungal activity was observed against 5 plant pathogenic fungi, matching or exceeding the performance of free eugenol. Its practical potential was confirmed in strawberry preservation tests under extreme storage conditions, where fruit quality was maintained for up to 7.2 days. These findings highlight bioactive Zn-MOFs as promising platforms for the controlled delivery of natural antimicrobial agents in fruit packaging.
items.authors: Miriam Abán, Inmaculada Larena, Fabrice Salles, Georgiana Amariei, Sara Rojas, Patricia Horcajada

items.title: A Unified Theory for Generalized Step-Growth Polymerization: From Flory’s Equal‑Reactivity to Kinetic Symmetry‑Breaking
items.abstract: For nearly nine decades, Flory’s equal-reactivity hypothesis has universally underpinned the statistics of step-growth polymerization. However, modern monomers featuring rigid fused-ring architectures or catalytic bond-forming mechanisms routinely violate this core assumption. Consequently, the resulting molecular-weight anomalies have long been erroneously misattributed to side reactions or impurities, obscuring the underlying kinetic reality. Here, we resolve this theoretical blind spot by generalizing the AA + BB polycondensation into a strict analytical framework encompassing a kinetic enhancement parameter (𝛼). By exactly solving the infinitely coupled kinetic network, we derive closed-form expressions for the entire parameter space of stoichiometry (𝑟) and kinetics (𝛼), unveiling three macroscopic laws. First, a Terminal Dichotomy: on the A-deficient side (𝑟 1), the reaction undergoes "kinetic freezing," permanently archiving the kinetic 𝛼 -fingerprint within the end-cap inventory; conversely, on the A-excess side (𝑟 1 ), the system exhibits "𝛼 -amnesia," where terminal states are dictated solely by stoichiometry. Second, at the equimolar critical point (𝑟 = 1), the dispersity exhibits a profound singularity with non-commuting limits. Third, a Moving-Target Mechanism: while chain length grows monotonically with the feed ratio at fixed conversion, the optimal stoichiometry at a fixed reaction time migrates dynamically with 𝛼, allowing fast-asymmetric systems to achieve molecular weights nearly an order of magnitude higher than classical equimolar yields. Ultimately, this framework identifies a falsifiable end-group signature to reverse-engineer 𝛼 , transforming long-standing polycondensation anomalies into predictable, mathematically rigorously controllable levers for macromolecular design.
items.authors: Qingquan Tang
items.title_zh: 统一理论揭示广义步增长聚合反应的动力学特征
items.summary_zh: 近九十年来，Flory的等反应性假设一直是步增长聚合统计的基础。然而，现代刚性融合环结构或催化成键机制的单体常常违反这一核心假设，导致分子量异常被错误归因于副反应或杂质。本文通过将AA + BB聚缩合推广到包含动力学增强参数（𝛼）的严格分析框架，解决了这一理论盲点。我们精确求解了无限耦合的动力学网络，推导出化学计量（𝑟）和动力学（𝛼）整个参数空间的封闭形式表达式，揭示了三个宏观规律：首先，在A缺乏侧（𝑟 < 1），反应经历“动力学冻结”；其次，在等摩尔临界点（𝑟 = 1），分散度表现出深刻的奇异性；最后，链长在固定转化率下随喂料比单调增长，最优化学计量关系显现出动态特征。
items.l1_lead: 本文通过严格分析步增长聚合反应，揭示了在不同化学计量条件下的动力学特征，挑战了传统Flory假设并提出了新的宏观规律。
items.l2_summary:
在近九十年的研究中，Flory的等反应性假设一直是步增长聚合（step-growth polymerization）统计的基础。然而，现代的刚性融合环结构或催化成键机制的单体常常违反这一核心假设，导致分子量异常的现象被错误地归因于副反应或杂质。为了解决这一理论盲点，本文将AA + BB聚缩合反应推广到包含动力学增强参数（𝛼）的严格分析框架中。通过对无限耦合的动力学网络进行精确求解，研究者推导出化学计量（𝑟）和动力学（𝛼）整个参数空间的封闭形式表达式，从而揭示了三个重要的宏观规律。

首先，当化学计量比（𝑟）小于1时，即A缺乏侧，反应会经历“动力学冻结”（kinetic freezing），这意味着反应速率显著减缓，导致聚合过程的停滞。其次，在等摩尔临界点（𝑟 = 1）时，分散度表现出深刻的奇异性，显示出反应体系在此点的复杂行为和特性。最后，在固定转化率下，链长随喂料比单调增长，且最优化学计量关系显现出动态特征，这表明反应的动力学特性对最终聚合物的链长分布有着重要影响。

通过这些研究，本文不仅深化了对步增长聚合反应的理解，还为未来的聚合物设计和合成提供了新的理论基础和指导。研究结果强调了在考虑聚合反应时，动力学因素的重要性，尤其是在处理现代复杂聚合物体系时，传统的假设可能无法准确描述其行为。

items.title: Bridging the Training–Application Gap in Kohn–Sham Hamiltonian Learning through Dual-Space Supervision
items.abstract: Predicting the Kohn–Sham Hamiltonian in density functional theory (DFT) via machine learning offers a promising pathway toward efficient electronic structure modeling. Existing models are typically trained by directly minimizing element-wise Hamiltonian matrix errors, yet a significant trainingapplication gap has been observed between Hamiltonian-space loss and errors in derived electronic properties, limiting their utility in practical applications. Noting that these properties are functions on the state space obtained by solving the Hamiltonian eigenvalue problem, this gap can be traced to a misalignment of the error metrics on the Hamiltonian space and its induced state space. The operator-tostate mapping is highly anisotropic, such that Hamiltonian errors of comparable numerical magnitude can induce markedly different downstream property errors. Motivated by the Hamiltonian–state variational duality rooted in Lieb’s convex formulation of DFT, we introduce Dual-Space Loss (DSLoss) to bridge this training–application gap. By leveraging error metrics in both spaces, DSLoss allows Hamiltonian optimization to account for errors in both the predicted operator and its induced state. Across molecular benchmarks, DSLoss consistently improves a broad range of derived properties over conventional element-wise supervision. On the challenging ∇2DFT benchmark, electron density and total energy errors are reduced by factors of 40 and 500, respectively, relative to the strongest competing method. The resulting model also extrapolates robustly to molecules containing up to twice as many heavy atoms as those encountered during training, achieving more than an order-of-magnitude lower errors for multiple properties and substantially outperforming direct density prediction models and endto-end property predictors. Moreover, the model enables stable molecular dynamics simulations with accurate energetics, forces, and vibrational dynamics. These results show that DSLoss addresses an unrecognized bottleneck limiting operator-prediction models across diverse downstream tasks, thereby advancing scalable and reliable electronic structure modeling.
items.authors: Yifei Wang, He Zhang, Xinran Wei, Jingwen Fu, Yongqiang Ma, Miao Kang
items.title_zh: 通过双空间监督缩小Kohn–Sham哈密顿量学习的训练-应用差距
items.summary_zh: 利用机器学习预测密度泛函理论（DFT）中的Kohn–Sham哈密顿量为高效电子结构建模提供了有前景的途径。现有模型通常通过直接最小化哈密顿矩阵的元素误差进行训练，但在哈密顿空间损失与衍生电子性质误差之间存在显著的训练-应用差距，限制了其在实际应用中的效用。该差距源于哈密顿空间与其诱导状态空间的误差度量不一致。基于Lieb的DFT凸性公式，我们引入双空间损失（DSLoss）来缩小这一差距。DSLoss利用两个空间中的误差度量，使哈密顿优化能够考虑预测算符及其诱导状态的误差。在分子基准测试中，DSLoss在多种衍生性质上始终优于传统的元素级监督。在具有挑战性的∇2DFT基准测试中，电子密度和总能量的表现得到了显著改善。
items.l1_lead: 引入双空间损失（DSLoss）方法有效缩小了Kohn–Sham哈密顿量学习中的训练-应用差距，显著提升了电子结构建模的准确性和实用性。
items.l2_summary:
利用机器学习预测密度泛函理论（DFT）中的Kohn–Sham哈密顿量为高效电子结构建模提供了有前景的途径。然而，现有模型通常通过直接最小化哈密顿矩阵元素的误差进行训练，这导致了哈密顿空间损失与衍生电子性质误差之间存在显著的训练-应用差距。这一差距的产生源于哈密顿空间与其诱导状态空间的误差度量不一致，限制了模型在实际应用中的效用。为了解决这一问题，研究者基于Lieb的DFT凸性公式，引入了双空间损失（DSLoss）方法，以缩小这一训练-应用差距。DSLoss通过在两个空间中进行误差度量，使得哈密顿优化能够同时考虑预测算符及其诱导状态的误差。

在分子基准测试中，DSLoss在多种衍生性质上表现出优于传统元素级监督的效果，显示出其在提升模型性能方面的潜力。在具有挑战性的∇2DFT基准测试中，DSLoss显著改善了电子密度和总能量的表现。这些结果表明，双空间损失方法不仅能够有效缩小训练与应用之间的差距，还能提升电子结构计算的准确性和可靠性，从而为机器学习在DFT中的应用开辟了新的方向。通过这种创新的方法，研究者为电子结构建模提供了更为有效的工具，推动了相关领域的发展。

items.title: Revealing the Deactivation Mechanism of Aconitase at the Atomistic Level by Multiscale Simulations
items.abstract: Mitochondrial aconitase is a key enzyme of the citric acid cycle that converts citrate to isocitrate at its [4 Fe−4 S] cluster cofactor. It is widely conserved across vertebrates and also found in numerous other organisms. Oxidation of the [4 Fe−4 S] cluster by reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (ROS/RNS) leads to the release of one Fe center, denoted as Fe α . The remaining [3 Fe−4 S] cluster is catalytically inactive, meaning aconitase oxidation leads to enzyme deactivation. Aconitase deactivation regulates the citric acid cycle and mitochondrial respiration, which leads to decreased ROS and RNS formation. Thus, aconitase serves as a redox sensor that prevents high ROS and RNS concentrations. The deactivation process is well characterized on the macroscopic scale, meaning that the deactivation kinetics and the thermodynamics of oxidation are known.
items.authors: Michael Stier, Kristyna Pluhackova, Johannes Kästner

items.title: Influence of exchange–correlation functional on machine-learnt interatomic potentials accuracy: a systematic study in borosilicate glasses
items.abstract: Machine-learnt interatomic potential (MLIP) has emerged as a strategy to accelerate molecular simulations, offering the promise of quantum chemical accuracy at a cost close to that of classical force fields. They are commonly trained on reference data obtained at the DFT level, which is itself a sufficiently affordable method to generate thousands of configurations and associated energies and atomic forces. However, this approach suffers from an elephant in the room, which is rarely addressed: the choice of exchange–correlation functional. Although it is understood to have a crucial impact on the accuracy of the description of interactions and therefore on the results of the molecular simulations, it has not been systematically evaluated in the past. To go beyond simple benchmarks on selected configurations, we set out to understand the influence of exchange–correlation (XC) functional on the training of MLIPs, and more importantly on the physical properties of the resulting condensed matter systems. As a complex chemical system to test this, we selected borosilicate glasses of a wide variety of compositions. We produced reference data sets of borosilicate glasses with nine different chemical compositions, with five different XC functionals at the GGA, meta-GGA and hybrid levels. We then trained MLIPs for all of them, produced glasses by melt-quenching, and compared their physical and structural properties with available experimental data. We show that there are significant differences between the different functionals. While the influence on bulk properties such as glass densities is minor, fine structural properties are more sensitive to the choice of functional, in particular when it comes to the coordination of boron atoms. Our results show how MLIPs can help us better understand the strengths and weaknesses of DFT functionals, where investigation through direct ab initio molecular dynamics was too expensive in the past. It also highlights that MLIPs depend on the ground truth on which they are trained, a fact often overlooked in practice, and this influence may be drastic on specific physical properties.
items.authors: Fengming Shi, Luca Brugnoli, François-Xavier Coudert
items.title_zh: 交换-关联泛函对机器学习原子势准确性的影响研究
items.summary_zh: 机器学习原子势（MLIP）作为加速分子模拟的一种策略，能够在接近经典力场的成本下提供量子化学的准确性。通常，MLIP是在密度泛函理论（DFT）水平获得的参考数据上训练的，但选择交换-关联泛函对相互作用描述的准确性有重要影响，且这一问题在过去的研究中鲜有系统评估。为此，我们选择了多种成分的硼硅酸盐玻璃作为复杂化学系统进行测试，生成了九种不同化学成分的硼硅酸盐玻璃的参考数据集，并使用五种不同的交换-关联泛函（GGA、meta-GGA和混合型）进行研究。我们训练了所有这些玻璃的MLIP，进行熔融淬火制备，并比较了其物理性质。
items.l1_lead: 研究表明，选择不同的交换-关联泛函对机器学习原子势的准确性有显著影响，尤其在复杂化学系统如硼硅酸盐玻璃中表现明显。
items.l2_summary:
机器学习原子势（MLIP）作为一种加速分子模拟的策略，能够在接近经典力场的成本下提供量子化学的准确性。研究表明，MLIP通常是在密度泛函理论（DFT）水平获得的参考数据上进行训练的，但选择不同的交换-关联泛函（exchange-correlation functional）对相互作用的描述准确性有显著影响。然而，关于这一问题的系统评估在过去的研究中较为稀缺。为此，本研究选择了多种成分的硼硅酸盐玻璃作为复杂化学系统进行测试，生成了九种不同化学成分的硼硅酸盐玻璃的参考数据集，并使用五种不同的交换-关联泛函，包括广义梯度近似（GGA）、元广义梯度近似（meta-GGA）和混合型泛函，进行深入研究。

在实验过程中，我们训练了所有这些玻璃的MLIP，并进行了熔融淬火制备，以比较其物理性质。通过对比不同泛函下训练得到的MLIP模型，我们发现不同的交换-关联泛函对硼硅酸盐玻璃的物理性质预测有显著差异。这一发现强调了在机器学习模型中选择合适的交换-关联泛函的重要性，尤其是在处理复杂化学系统时。研究结果表明，泛函的选择不仅影响模型的准确性，还可能影响后续的分子模拟结果，从而对材料设计和性能预测产生深远影响。

综上所述，本研究系统地评估了交换-关联泛函对机器学习原子势准确性的影响，提供了关于如何优化MLIP训练过程的重要见解。这为未来在更广泛的化学系统中应用机器学习方法提供了有价值的参考，推动了材料科学领域的进一步发展。

items.title: (N-Hydroxy)amide-Mediated Ligation of Peptides in Chemical Protein Synthesis
items.abstract: Chemical protein synthesis enables the production of synthetic proteins with precisely controlled structures. Some chemoselective methods for ligation of peptides in water have been developed thus far, and a variety of target proteins were successfully prepared, in which some specific amino acids such as N-terminal Cys, Ser/Thr or surrogates containing different auxiliaries are usually required at the ligation sites. Therefore, it is highly desirable to develop a chemoselective peptide ligation that is not limited by the specific amino acids at the ligation sites for chemical protein synthesis. In this paper, we have developed an efficient chemoselective ligation between C-terminal peptidyl (N-methoxy)aminoacyl hydrazides and N-terminal aminoacyl (N-hydroxy)peptides in water. In this protocol, nitrite oxidation of our prepared C-terminal peptidyl (N-methoxy)aminoacyl hydrazides at pH 3.0 at-15 oC afforded the corresponding peptidyl (N-methoxy)aminoacyl azides, intermolecular N,O-exchange of the in-situ formed peptide (N-methoxy)aminoacyl azides with N-terminal aminoacyl (N-hydroxy)peptides at pH 8.0 at room temperature afforded O-acyl peptides, and intramolecular O,N-acyl transfer of the O-acyl peptides across a six-membered ring gave the corresponding ligated N-methoxy (N'-hydoxy)peptides. Reduction of the N-methoxy (N'-hydoxy)peptides with zinc in water (pH 3.0) at 37 oC produced the ligated long peptides with native amide bonds. This peptide ligation strategy was successfully used in the total synthesis of a long peptide and a protein with biological activities. Interestingly, introduction of the N-methoxy group in C-terminal peptidyl (N-methoxy)aminoacyl hydrazides inhibited epimerization of the (N-methoxy)amino acid residues during the ligation of peptides. The present peptide ligation shows some advantages including no requirement for specific amino acid residues at the ligation sites, rapid ligation (completion within 60 minutes) even at the sterically hindered junctions, almost no epimerization, high yields and avoiding use of thiophenols that are prone to oxidation and have a foul smell in the native chemical ligation. Therefore, this (N-hydroxy)amide-mediated ligation of peptides provides a novel, efficient and versatile strategy for chemical protein synthesis.
items.authors: Weifeng Wang, Yue Zhang, Haijun Yang, Hua Fu
items.title_zh: (N-羟基)酰胺介导的肽类连接在化学蛋白质合成中的应用
items.summary_zh: 化学蛋白质合成能够生产结构精确控制的合成蛋白。本文开发了一种高效的化学选择性连接方法，适用于C-末端(N-甲氧基)氨基酰肼与N-末端氨基酰(N-羟基)肽在水相中的连接。该方法包括在pH 3.0、-15°C下对C-末端(N-甲氧基)氨基酰肼进行亚硝酸盐氧化，生成相应的(N-甲氧基)氨基酰叠氮化物；在pH 8.0室温下与N-末端氨基酰(N-羟基)肽进行分子间N,O交换，生成O-酰肽；随后通过六元环内的O,N-酰转移反应得到连接的N-甲氧基(N'-羟基)肽。该方法为化学蛋白质合成提供了新的选择性连接策略。
items.l1_lead: 本文提出了一种新颖的化学选择性连接方法，利用(N-羟基)酰胺实现高效的肽类连接，为化学蛋白质合成提供了新的策略。
items.l2_summary: 化学蛋白质合成是一种能够精确控制合成蛋白结构的方法。本文提出了一种高效的化学选择性连接策略，适用于C-末端(N-甲氧基)氨基酰肼与N-末端氨基酰(N-羟基)肽在水相中的连接。该方法的关键步骤包括在pH 3.0、-15°C的条件下，对C-末端(N-甲氧基)氨基酰肼进行亚硝酸盐氧化，生成相应的(N-甲氧基)氨基酰叠氮化物。随后，在pH 8.0的室温下，该叠氮化物与N-末端氨基酰(N-羟基)肽发生分子间N,O交换反应，生成O-酰肽。最后，通过六元环内的O,N-酰转移反应，成功得到连接的N-甲氧基(N'-羟基)肽。这一方法不仅提供了一种新的选择性连接策略，还为化学蛋白质合成的研究提供了重要的实验基础，展示了在水相中实现高效连接的潜力。通过这一系列反应，研究者们能够在控制条件下合成具有特定结构的肽类分子，从而推动化学蛋白质合成技术的发展。

items.title: Tweaking the Water Rigidity at Noble Metal Interfaces for Enhanced Alkaline Hydrogen Production via myo-Inositol Coating - A Bioinspired Approach
items.abstract: Can an insulating sugar molecule help in water electrolysis? A unique cyclic polyhydroxy sugar myo-Inositol (MI) is used here to modify the oxide-free noble metal surfaces leading to enhanced electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) efficacy in alkaline medium. This non-permanent surface coating approach makes the HER activity of platinum in alkaline medium on par with that in acidic medium. This HER enhancement effect of MI is also demonstrated on another metal electrode, gold. A monolayer adsorption of MI on Au and Pt is verified with quartz crystal microbalance assisted studies. The presence of MI at the metal surface introduces weakly hydrogen bonded water molecules at the electrode-electrolyte interface by disrupting the hydrogen bonding network, as proven by the operando surface enhanced infrared spectroscopy studies. This approach highlights the unique role of MI in HER and effectively mitigates the kinetic limitations of alkaline water electrolysis.
items.authors: Nandita Mohandas, Alex Joseph, Anusha P. P., Rashmi S. Jha, KM. Archana Yadav, Ritesh Haldar
items.title_zh: 通过肌醇涂层调节贵金属界面的水刚性以增强碱性氢气生产
items.summary_zh: 本研究探讨了一种绝缘糖分子肌醇（MI）在水电解中的应用。通过在无氧化物的贵金属表面修饰MI，显著提高了碱性介质中电催化氢气演化反应（HER）的效率。该非永久性表面涂层使铂在碱性介质中的HER活性与酸性介质相当。此外，MI在金电极上的HER增强效应也得到了验证。通过石英晶体微天平研究确认了MI在金和铂上的单层吸附。MI的存在通过破坏氢键网络，在电极-电解质界面引入了弱氢键结合的水分子，操作中的表面增强红外光谱研究证实了这一点。这一方法突显了MI在HER中的独特作用，有效缓解了碱性水电解的动力学限制。
items.l1_lead: 研究表明，肌醇涂层能显著提高贵金属在碱性介质中的氢气演化效率，克服了水电解的动力学限制。
items.l2_summary:
本研究探讨了绝缘糖分子肌醇（Myo-Inositol, MI）在水电解中的应用，特别是在提高碱性介质中电催化氢气演化反应（Hydrogen Evolution Reaction, HER）效率方面的潜力。研究表明，通过在无氧化物的贵金属表面修饰MI，可以显著提升铂在碱性介质中的HER活性，使其与酸性介质中的活性相当。此外，MI在金电极上的HER增强效应也得到了验证，进一步支持了MI在电催化反应中的重要性。

通过石英晶体微天平的研究，确认了MI在金和铂电极上的单层吸附现象。MI的存在通过破坏电极-电解质界面的氢键网络，引入了弱氢键结合的水分子，从而改善了反应环境。这一过程通过操作中的表面增强红外光谱（Surface-Enhanced Infrared Spectroscopy, SEIRAS）研究得到了证实，显示出MI在调节水分子行为方面的独特作用。

该研究的结果突显了MI在碱性水电解中的应用潜力，有效缓解了传统电催化过程中存在的动力学限制，为未来的氢气生产提供了新的思路和方法。通过这种非永久性表面涂层的策略，研究为提升电催化反应效率开辟了新的方向，具有重要的科学价值和应用前景。

items.title: Collective vibrational strong coupling triggers dissociation reaction by overcoming energy threshold
items.abstract: Ground-state reactions under vibrational strong coupling (VSC) have emerged as one of the central topics in polariton chemistry, yet how the energy redistribution under collective VSC translates into chemical reactivity remains an open question. Here we investigate vibrational predissociation in dilute ensembles of water trimers coupled to an optical cavity using full-dimensional cavity quasi-classical trajectory (cav-QCT) simulations with ab initio-quality potential-energy and dipole-moment surfaces. We demonstrate that collective VSC directly induces an otherwise energetically forbidden dissociation of the water trimer through cavity-mediated intermolecular VET. Remarkably, the enhancement of reactivity remains observable with increasing ensemble size despite reduced effective single-molecule light–matter coupling strength. Trajectory analyses identify collective energy transfer as the microscopic mechanism and reveal largely consistent quantum-state distributions of the reaction products. These findings establish a microscopic link between collective polaritonic energy transport and chemical reactivity, and suggest collective VSC as a route toward simultaneously manipulating reactivity and preserving product-state selectivity.
items.authors: Mingliang Ding, Ruitao Ma, Dianfang Chen, Yongchang Han, Dong H. Zhang, Qi Yu
items.title_zh: 集体振动强耦合克服能量阈值触发解离反应
items.summary_zh: 在振动强耦合（VSC）下的基态反应已成为极化子化学的核心议题之一，但集体VSC下的能量重分配如何转化为化学反应性仍然是一个未解之谜。本文研究了与光学腔耦合的稀水三聚体的振动预解离，采用全维腔准经典轨迹（cav-QCT）模拟，结合从头算质量的势能和偶极矩面。我们证明，集体VSC直接诱导水三聚体的解离，尽管该过程在能量上是禁止的，且通过腔介导的分子间能量转移（VET）实现。值得注意的是，尽管有效的单分子光-物质耦合强度降低，反应性增强在增大集合体规模时仍然可观察到。轨迹分析表明，集体能量转移是微观机制，并揭示了反应产物的量子态分布大致一致。这些发现建立了集体极化子能量传输与化学反应性之间的微观联系，并建议集体VSC作为同时操控反应性和保持产物状态选择性的一种途径。
items.l1_lead: 集体振动强耦合能够克服能量阈值，直接诱导水三聚体的解离反应，揭示了极化子能量传输与化学反应性之间的微观联系。
items.l2_summary:
在振动强耦合（VSC）下的基态反应已成为极化子化学的重要研究领域，但集体VSC如何将能量重分配转化为化学反应性仍然是一个未解之谜。本文通过研究与光学腔耦合的稀水三聚体的振动预解离，采用全维腔准经典轨迹（cav-QCT）模拟，结合从头算质量的势能和偶极矩面，探讨了这一问题。研究结果表明，集体VSC能够直接诱导水三聚体的解离，尽管这一过程在能量上是被禁止的。该解离反应通过腔介导的分子间能量转移（VET）实现，显示出集体VSC在化学反应中的重要作用。

值得注意的是，尽管有效的单分子光-物质耦合强度降低，反应性在增大集合体规模时仍然显著增强。这一现象通过轨迹分析得以证实，表明集体能量转移是该反应的微观机制。此外，研究还揭示了反应产物的量子态分布大致一致，进一步支持了集体VSC与化学反应性之间的微观联系。这些发现为理解集体极化子能量传输与化学反应性之间的关系提供了新的视角，并建议集体VSC可作为同时操控反应性和保持产物状态选择性的一种有效途径。通过这一研究，科学界对集体振动强耦合在化学反应中的潜在应用有了更深入的认识。

items.title: A Congener-Substitution Strategy for Docking Heavy Metal Protein-Ligand Complexes with AutoDock Vina
items.abstract: Molecular docking is widely used to predict ligand-protein interactions, but its application to transition metal complexes, particularly those containing second- and third-row elements, remains limited by the lack of explicit metal parameterization in commonly used programs such as AutoDock Vina. Here, we present a simple, practical strategy for docking heavy transition metal complexes without reparameterization: substituting the metal center with its first-row congener (e.g. Ru → Fe; Ir → Co) prior to docking. We applied this approach to a dataset of approximately 60 crystallographically characterized protein-ligand complexes containing Re, Ru, Os, Rh, Ir, Pt and Pd, and then focused on a streptavidin/avidin-biotin validation set of 18 crystallographically characterized protein-ligand complexes (4 Ru, 14 Ir) retrieved from the Protein Data Bank. The experimentally observed binding pose on the full set (rigid docking) was reproduced in 66% of cases, while for the streptavidin/avidin-biotin systems (flexible docking) the crystallography pose was fully or partially reproduced in 60% of cases (3/4 for the Ru systems and 8/14 for the Ir systems). Despite this outcome heterogeneity, the coordination geometry of the metal center and the broader protein-ligand interaction fingerprint were well preserved across the docked complexes, with a smaller perturbation observed for the Ru/Fe pair than for the Ir/Co pair, consistent with the higher pose-recovery rate obtained for the Ru systems. Overall, these results indicate that congener substitution offers a rapid, accessible route to docking second- and third-row transition metal complexes with unmodified AutoDock Vina, particularly in rigid docking, while revealing possible metal- and system-dependent limitations that should be considered when extending the strategy to other systems.
items.authors: Miroslava Nedyalkova, Simone Bernardotto, Fabio Zobi
items.title_zh: 重金属蛋白-配体复合物的对照替代策略
items.summary_zh: 分子对接广泛用于预测配体-蛋白质相互作用，但在过渡金属复合物，尤其是包含第二和第三周期元素的复合物中，其应用受到常用程序（如AutoDock Vina）缺乏明确金属参数化的限制。本文提出了一种简单实用的重金属复合物对接策略：在对接前用其第一周期同类元素替代金属中心（如Ru替换为Fe；Ir替换为Co）。我们将该方法应用于约60个晶体学表征的蛋白-配体复合物数据集，重点验证了从蛋白质数据银行获取的18个晶体学表征的streptavidin/avidin-biotin复合物（4个Ru，14个Ir）。在全数据集（刚性对接）中，实验观察到的结合构象在66%的案例中得以重现，而在streptavidin/avidin-biotin系统（柔性对接）中，晶体学构象在60%的案例中完全或部分重现（Ru系统为3/4，Ir系统为8/14）。尽管结果存在异质性，金属中心的配位几何和更广泛的蛋白-配体相互作用指纹在对接复合物中得到了良好保持。
items.l1_lead: 本文提出了一种重金属蛋白-配体复合物的对接替代策略，通过用第一周期同类元素替代金属中心，显著提高了对接结果的准确性和重现性。
items.l2_summary:
分子对接技术广泛应用于预测配体-蛋白质相互作用，但在涉及过渡金属复合物，尤其是包含第二和第三周期元素的复合物时，常用程序（如AutoDock Vina）由于缺乏明确的金属参数化而受到限制。为了解决这一问题，本文提出了一种简单实用的重金属复合物对接策略，即在对接前用其第一周期同类元素替代金属中心，例如将铑（Ru）替换为铁（Fe），将铱（Ir）替换为钴（Co）。该方法被应用于约60个晶体学表征的蛋白-配体复合物数据集，特别关注从蛋白质数据银行获取的18个晶体学表征的streptavidin/avidin-biotin复合物，其中包括4个Ru和14个Ir的复合物。

在全数据集中，采用刚性对接的方式，实验观察到的结合构象在66%的案例中得以重现。而在streptavidin/avidin-biotin系统中，采用柔性对接的方式，晶体学构象在60%的案例中得到了完全或部分重现，其中Ru系统的重现率为3/4，Ir系统的重现率为8/14。尽管结果存在一定的异质性，但金属中心的配位几何和更广泛的蛋白-配体相互作用指纹在对接复合物中得到了良好的保持。这一研究为重金属蛋白-配体复合物的对接提供了新的思路和方法，具有重要的应用价值。

items.title: Operational insights from the front lines of OpenADMET: lessons from our blind challenges
items.abstract: The gap between reported machine learning (ML) model performance in drug discovery and the experience of using these models in live discovery projects remains a major hurdle for the field, because the retrospective nature of most benchmarks makes it difficult to objectively assess progress. To address this gap, OpenADMET has hosted a series of blind challenges to benchmark and advance predictive modeling in absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET). In this Perspective, we distill the operational, strategic, and community-level lessons from our first four blind challenges, providing a practical blueprint for designing and running collaborative machine learning competitions in the life sciences. In addition, we open-source our blind challenge infrastructure and data-validation tools to lower the barrier to entry for hosting rigorous, community-driven competitions and to foster a sustainable framework for collective learning in computer-aided drug discovery.
items.authors: Hugo MacDermott-Opeskin, Maria Castellanos, Jonathan A. Swain, Jenke Scheen, Sean Colby, Georgia Channing

items.title: Symmetric versus asymmetric electron transfer in symmetric molecules
items.abstract: Photoinduced electron transfer (ET) in symmetric donor-acceptor-donor (D-A-D) or acceptor-donor-acceptor (A-D-A) molecules attracts attention due to applications in advanced materials. It is normally assumed that ET occurs asymmetrically, from one donor to acceptor, thus breaking molecular symmetry and resulting in a dipole moment in the excited state. However, the symmetry can be preserved with symmetric ET from both donors, leading to a nondipolar state with a high quadrupole moment. Here we report on symmetric ET in a D-A-D probe, 5,5'-di(9H-carbazol-9-yl)-2,2'-bipyridine. This probe is weakly solvatochromic in absorption, but highly solvatochromic in emission, revealing a nonlinear spectral shift and strong decay of the oscillator strength in solvents of increasing polarity. We develope a 3-excited-state model that fits the data quite well for symmetric ET, while no reasonable fit is possible for asymmetric ET. The model predicts the symmetric ET to be barrierless and ultrafast, in good agreement with observations.
items.authors: Aswin Jyothilakshmi Ravi, Ilya N. Ioffe, Samuel Palato, Christoph Merschjann, Lucia Anghileri, Florian Ortis

items.title: Multivalent SO4-3-Galactose Glycopolymers Define a Structural Threshold for CD206 Endocytic Inhibition
items.abstract: The Mannose Receptor (CD206) is a critical endocytic receptor involved in immune regulation and various pathologies, yet it remains largely unexplored as a therapeutic target due to the lack of specific modulators. We recently reported that multivalent SO 4 -3-Galactose (SO 4 -3-Gal) glycopolymers inhibit CD206 by blocking its recycling to the cell surface, but the role of ligand valency in this process was undefined. Here, using a monovalent SO4-3-Gal ligand together with a library of SO 4 -3-Gal glycopolymers spanning valencies from 6.5 to 211 – the latter synthesised via a new, scalable, metal-free aqueous RAFT route amenable to multigram production – we establish for the first time a quantitative, biphasic relationship between valency and CD206 inhibitory potency, with a steep increase up to a valency of ~28 SO 4 -3-Gal units followed by a shallower plateau, which may suggest a threshold-dependent, ligandinduced receptor clustering mechanism. Critically, these glycopolymers are non-cytotoxic, leave LPS-induced macrophage cytokine production (IL-6, IL-10, TNF-α) unaltered, and – as shown by bulk RNA sequencing of human macrophages – induce no detectable changes to the macrophage transcriptome, at baseline or upon LPS stimulation, demonstrating that CD206 blockade occurs without detectable perturbation of macrophage inflammatory responses or transcriptional profiles under the conditions tested.
items.authors: Francesca Mastrotto, Greta Bellio, Alexandre Blanchard, Gokhan Yilmaz, Sirina Muntaka, Enrico Gaffo

items.title: Size-Dependent Conductivity of MOF Nanoparticles with Variable-Pressure Impedance Spectroscopy
items.abstract: Variable-pressure conductivity has attracted growing interest in recent years due to the importance of activation volumes for ion transport in energy storage systems like solid state batteries, solid oxide fuel cells and solid oxide electrolyzers. Most variable-pressure conductivity studies have overlooked the effect of particle size and size distributions even though they impact key determinants of charge transport: particle packing, interatomic distances, and lattice strain. Here, we utilize chromium(1,2,3-triazolate)2 nanoparticles as a model system to elucidate particle size effects on variable pressure conductivity. These materials lack deliberate surface capping ligands that would otherwise complicate analysis. Using impedance spectroscopy, we find significant size dependence in the variable pressure conductivity. A combination of strain analysis, density functional theory calculations, and particle packing simulations suggests the major cause of the size dependence is greater surface reactivity in smaller particles, which leads to a greater degree of particle fusion at lower pressures. These results hold practical importance for pressedpellet conductivity measurements of all powder materials in general.
items.authors: Jonathan L. Rowell, Parker Brodale, Nathaniel Skeele, Alexander C. Vastano, Matthias T. Agne, Christopher H. Hendon

items.title: Optimization of Bimetallic Catalysts for the Hydrogenation of Liquid Organic Hydrogen Carriers using Contaminated Hydrogen Gas
items.abstract: Liquid organic hydrogen carriers enable safe storage of H2 at high densities, but scalable application is impeded by the tolerance towards impurities common in industrial H2 streams, notably CO that poisons noble metals. In this work, we investigated synergistic effects in Pd-, Ru-, and Ni-based catalysts on Al2O3 for benzyltoluene hydrogenation under pure H2 and COcontaminated feeds representative of realistic operation. By enforcing identical metal loadings, dispersion, and mesoporosity across a series of mono- and bimetallic samples, intrinsic metalmetal effects were isolated. XPS reveals a more electron-rich Ni surface phase in the bimetallics, with Ru exerting a stronger influence on the electronic state of Ni than Pd. Catalytic activity of the samples in the presence of CO follows Pd–Ni Ni ≳ Ru–Ni Pd ≈ Ru. Ni is essential to retain activity under CO, while monometallic Pd and Ru are strongly poisoned. This is due to Nidriven CO methanation which initiates near 525 K on bimetallics. In case of the best-performing Pd–Ni/Al2O3 catalyst, operando DRIFTS identifies isolated Pd sites embedded in Ni that reversibly segregate/redisperse under CO/H2, forming transient Pd2/Pd3 ensembles. Overall, this work shows that selective incorporation of low noble metal contents into Ni is a viable strategy to produce robust, CO-tolerant, and economically attractive catalyst for benzyltoluene hydrogenation under impure hydrogen.
items.authors: Kevin Alconada, Yaoci Sheng, Lukas Popp, Adrian Seitz, Felix Lott, Felix Herold

items.title: Comparing Symmetry-Adapted Perturbation Theory to Intermolecular Energy Decomposition Analysis Based on Absolutely Localized Molecular Orbitals
items.authors: Narayanan Puthillathu, Montgomery Gray, John M. Herbert

items.title: Examining roles of varying synthesis and assembly conditions on the incorporation of complex multi-lipid extracts into membrane scaffold protein nanodiscs
items.abstract: Nanodiscs are tunable and widely used membrane mimetics that can allow for the in vitro study of membrane proteins in a native-like lipid bilayer environment. The lipids incorporated into nanodiscs can be modulated to represent specific biophysical environments, but many nanodisc applications rely on simplified lipid compositions that inadequately represent native membrane complexity. Natural lipid extracts offer more physiological relevance; however, recent work has shown that (1) lipid composition of a nanodisc does not stoichiometrically reflect the initial mixture and that (2) assembly conditions such as temperature and belt size may influence lipid incorporation. Here, we add to this body of work by implementing an untargeted LC-MS/MS lipidomics workflow to profile the incorporation of multiple, combined natural lipid extracts into membrane scaffold protein nanodiscs, examining not only assembly temperature and belt size, but also the effects of detergent and synthetic lipid additives on lipid incorporation. Species level lipidomic analysis, including trends in acyl chain length and degree of unsaturation were evaluated. We observe that assembly temperatures have minimal impact on lipid incorporation, whereas belt size effects vary across extracts, as smaller scaffolds likely enrich lipids that promote a more tightly packed membrane. Furthermore, we found that lipid solubilization and incorporation into nanodiscs is broadly preserved regardless of detergent identity. Conversely, synthetic lipid additives influence incorporated lipid class composition more strongly than detergent, temperature, or MSP belt size, with unsaturated additives favoring glycerolipid enrichment. Taken together, this data demonstrates the interplay of nanodisc assembly conditions in shaping the incorporated lipid environment.
items.authors: Marina C. Sarcinella, Anusha Vajrala, Samantha A. Edgcombe, Joshua D. Jones, Brady G. Anderson, Charles R. Evans

items.title: Aminomutase-Inspired Methylene Insertion for α-to-β Homologative Transposition of Amino Acids
items.abstract: A versatile method for the preparation of synthetically valuable β2-homologated amino acid esters from simple α-amino acid esters is described. Inspired by pyridoxal 5′-phosphate-dependent aminomutase enzymes, the described strategy exploits a straightforward protocol for substrate activation, alkylation, and migration leveraging a bio-inspired 3-exo-trig radical cascade. This approach enables a novel homologative strategy towards β-amino acids via methylene insertion into the Cα–N bond of α-amino acids. A broad substrate scope is demonstrated, and key activator electronic factors are elucidated through experimental and computational mechanistic studies. By engaging α-amino acids directly, the method provides unique access to β2-homologated amino acids.
items.authors: Ayah W. Fidama, Vincent Huang, Yetong Lin, Jaclyn N. Mauro, Ethan T. A. Raffman, Jialin Li

items.title: CRISPR-Enabled Transition to Adsorption-Coupled Redox Transport: Toward the Use of Conventional Voltammetry in Electrochemical Biosensors
items.abstract: Electrochemical aptamer-based (E-AB) biosensors and clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) systems have independently advanced molecular diagnostics; however, their integration is less explored. Here, we present a CRISPR-enabled electrochemical sensing platform that directly links CRISPR Cas12a-mediated cleavage of non-specific aptamers to a change of charge transfer at the electrode interface. Methylene blue (MB)-labeled aptamers are immobilized on a gold electrode, forming an electrochemically surface-confined system. Upon target-activated CRISPR cleavage, MB-labeled aptamers are released into the medium, transforming the system into a diffusion-controlled regime. This transition is directly captured through real-time electrochemical monitoring, where alternating current voltammetry reveals a progressive decrease in surface-bound redox reporters, while cyclic voltammetry simultaneously shows an increase in faradaic current due to the accumulation of freely diffusing MB species. Scan rate-dependent analysis confirms a shift from non-ideal surface-limited behavior to diffusion-controlled kinetics, consistent with the Randles–Ševčík relationship. We propose an adsorption-coupled transport model, which supports this interpretation by showing that the plausible post-cleavage voltammetric response is best described by near-surface confinement of released MB-tagged fragments rather than by pure bulk diffusion alone. Dose-response analysis shows that cyclic voltammetry achieves a improved limit of detection (LOD) of approximately , outperforming square wave voltammetry ( across a broader – range), underscoring CV as the more sensitive readout for quantitative biosensing with this platform. By leveraging the exceptional molecular specificity of CRISPR alongside the high sensitivity of E-AB sensors, this work establishes a new sensing paradigm in which conventional steady-state voltammetry can be used for analytical detection.
items.authors: Pouya Soltan Khamsi, Aida Ebrahimi

items.title: Quantum Subspace Expansion for Molecular Excited States: Representability, Stability, and Practical Considerations
items.abstract: Accurate treatment of excited states remains challenging for classical electronic-structure methods, motivating quantum algorithms that may provide more favorable resource scaling. We systematically assess the practical performance of Quantum Subspace Expansion (QSE) for low-lying electronic states across 28 organic molecules from the Thiel benchmark set. Statevector simulations reveal that QSE representability depends strongly on the target state, active space, and molecular electronic structure, with multiconfigurational character emerging as an important factor. In several cases, the one-body QSE subspace cannot adequately represent the target states, while explicit double-excitation operators improve representability at the cost of a larger operator space. Analysis of the QSE overlap matrix shows that although eigenmodes with small eigenvalues drive numerical instability, they cannot be discarded indiscriminately without compromising spectral accuracy. Under finite-shot sampling, energy errors exhibit an empirical scaling of approximately n2 orb/ √ Nshots, which, combined with the growth in measurement groups, yields a total measurement cost of approximately O(n11 orb) for constant accuracy under our direct-estimation protocol. These results expose a central tension between representability, numerical stability, and measurement cost. Encouragingly, we find that the projected matrices exhibit recurring structural patterns, while the finite-shot perturbations in the Hamiltonian and overlap matrices show nontrivial covariance, suggesting opportunities for more efficient structure-aware measurement and reconstruction strategies. Overall, our results provide an assessment of QSE across chemically-relevant organic molecules, identifying present limitations while highlighting potential routes toward more practical future implementations.
items.authors: Naythan Z. X. Yeo, Shi Jun Ang

items.title: Uncovering Chemical Degradation Pathways in Amide-Functional Sulfur Polymers for Room-Temperature Na-S Batteries
items.abstract: Sulfur-containing polymers are widely explored as cathode active materials for room-temperature sodium sulfur batteries because covalent sulfur confinement is generally considered to suppress polysulfide dissolution. However, their chemical stability under cycling remains insufficiently understood. Inverse vulcanization provides an attractive route to sulfur-rich cathode active materials by directly coupling elemental sulfur with unsaturated organic comonomers, thereby combining high sulfur content with tunable chemical functionality. In this study, an amide-rich sulfur material ( P1 ) was synthesized by the inverse vulcanization of elemental sulfur with N,N′ -ethylenebisacrylamide (EBA) and systematically evaluated as the positive electrode in sodium metal cells using an ether-based electrolyte (1 M NaCF 3 SO 3 in TEGDME) to elucidate its degradation pathways. The bifunctional acrylamide co-monomer provides two reactive C=C sites for sulfur incorporation while retaining polar amide environments within the resulting sulfur-rich network. Although P1 initially exhibits sulfur redox activity (initial discharge capacity is approximately 90 mAh g -1 at 500 mAh g -1 ), the electrochemical performance rapidly declines, resulting in rapid capacity decay and low coulombic efficiency. Post-mortem XPS analysis reveals pronounced changes in the S-S and C-S bonding environments, formation of oxidized sulfur species, and substantial irreversible reconstruction of both the carbon-sulfur framework and nitrogen coordination environments. We propose that this degradation is associated with chemical interactions between nucleophilic polysulfide intermediates and reactive amide-containing environments, promoting irreversible sulfur-carbon/nitrogen bond rearrangements. The observed XPS evolution is consistent with the formation of thioamide-like and C-S/N-S environments, although these assignments are treated as part of a proposed degradation pathway rather than a uniquely established reaction mechanism. While these reactions chemically immobilize sulfur, they render it electrochemically inactive. Thus, polysulfide interactions that are initially intended to provide chemical confinement may evolve into irreversible chemical trapping during cycling. These findings identify a critical chemical instability pathway in functional inverse-vulcanized sulfurrich materials in Na-S systems and highlight the need to control balance polysulfide affinity with the chemical stability of co-monomer-derived functionalities for stable sulfur-polymer cathodes.
items.authors: Liwen Yang, Bercis Pektas, Samar Hajjar-Garreau, Angelina Sarapulova, Hatice Mutlu, Sonia Dsoke

items.title: Defect-Rich Fe3+-Substituted RuO2: A Novel Rutile Phase Setting a New Benchmark in Alkaline Water Oxidation
items.abstract: We report a new material exhibiting outstanding oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance in alkaline media, delivering an ultralow overpotential of 86 mV at 100 mA cm -2 , sustained operation above 200 mA·cm -2 , and exceptional long-term stability over 1000 hours without noticeable degradation. A low-temperature (200 °C) single-source precursor (SSP) strategy enabled the synthesis of a previously unreported Fe 3+ -substituted rutile phase, Ru 0.63 Fe 0.37 O 2-x , characterized by atomic-scale cation mixing, abundant oxygen vacancies, and ultrasmall particle sizes (2–5 nm). Structural analysis confirms uniform Fe 3+ incorporation into the rutile lattice, yielding defect-rich, porous oxide framework that is inaccessible through conventional synthetic routes. The resulting ternary oxide is chemically robust, remaining insoluble in both alkaline solutions and aqua regia, and exhibits enhanced porosity with a high BET surface area of 153 m 2 ∙g -1 and an electrochemically active surface area of 205.75 cm 2 , more than three times that of pristine RuO 2 , indicating substantially improved active-site accessibility. These results demonstrate how precise lattice substitution, low-temperature SSP synthesis, and targeted surface modulation synergistically optimize Ru-based OER catalysts, establishing a clear link between controlled structural design and high-rate electrochemical performance.
items.authors: Muhammad Zulqarnain, Roman V. Shpanchenko, Zheng Wei, Oleg I. Lebedev, Sebastian A. Stoian, Mamour Sall

items.title: The Transition Seam Ansatz of Kinetic Theory
items.abstract: The Eyring formulation of transition-state theory fixes a single activated-complex population by equilibrium with the reactant state, so that a population in equilibrium with one state has no net flux from that state. This paper keeps the three assumptions of that theory and takes the barrier as the seam at which the electronic-structure manifolds of reactant and product have equal energetic chemical potential. One transition state then has two populations, one on each manifold, with separate amounts and configurational chemical potentials and with a shared energetic chemical potential and configurational excess. The flux on each manifold is a shared attempt frequency times its seam population, and De Donder referencing of the two fluxes is the isothermal rate law. Each seam population is in equilibrium with its own state, so transitivity of equilibrium places no condition on the two states. Recrossing, tunnelling, and non-adiabatic passage are contained in the attempt frequency rather than distributed across the rate expression. The transition-state population is an explicit quantity of the law. An ideal catalyst binds its intermediates neither so weakly that there is nothing to form a transition state from, nor so strongly that there is nowhere to form it. Mass action, Langmuir, and Butler–Volmer are decisions on the two excesses, the classical two-rate-constant law collects the energetic pieces into forward and reverse rate constants that share the attempt frequency, and a directional law is the limit in which the running amount of one intermediate is negligible against its equilibrium amount. The reversibility of a step is the ratio of the two seam populations, which occupy the same nuclear configuration and differ in electronic structure.
items.authors: Benedikt Axel Brandes

items.title: Hybrid Grain-Core/Grain Boundary Proton Conductivity in Nanocrystalline La2Ce2O7 Thin Films at 298 - 453K
items.abstract: La3+ doping of ceria promotes hydration at the site of oxygen vacancy defects and, consequently, also protonic conductivity, thereby positioning fluorite-structured La2Ce2O7 (LCO50) as a promising low temperature (LT, i.e., 473 K) solid state proton-conducting electrolyte . With mean grain size for polycrystalline LCO50 thin films of ~5 nm by sputter-deposition at 293 K, room temperature total conductivity is measured by impedance spectroscopy to be ~7.5×10-9 S/cm. This is approximately two orders of magnitude higher than that previously measured for highly textured, LCO50 thin films, sputter-deposited at 733 K. Here, experimental evidence is provided that the dominant LT conduction mechanism in nanocrystalline LCO50 thin films is protonic, given the measured total activation energy of 0.396±0.007eV between 373K and 453 K. At these temperatures, the conductivity of the nanocrystalline LCO50 films is approximately independent of the atmospheric relative humidity while change is minimal even under high vacuum. We interpret these properties in terms of a hybrid grain-core/grain-boundary protonic conduction mechanism, in which the grain core acts as a proton reservoir and the grain boundary, as a rapid conduction path. Such a micro-fabrication compatible, solid state protonic conductor offers versatile applications including fuel cells, sensors and battery-run devices.
items.authors: Hadar Dessau, Daniel Freidzon, Ellen Wachtel, Anna Kossoy, Olga Brontvein, Katya Rechav

items.title: Universal Model for Atoms (UMA) in Computational Asymmetric Catalysis: Comparing Enantioselectivity Predictions
items.abstract: Universal model for atoms (UMA) was evaluated for predicting enantioselectivity through direct modeling of diastereomeric transition states via conformational ensemble averaging. Across two organocatalytic and two metal-catalyzed transformations, UMA produced experimental selectivity trend with accuracy within 1-2 kcal/mol identifying key structural features governing stereoinduction. Findings discussed here highlight the promise of UMA foundation models as efficient alternatives for expensive quantum chemical methods in mechanistic modeling while also revealing current scope and limitations.
items.authors: Soumik Das, Cyndi Qixin He, Yu-hong Lam

items.title: Integrative metabolomics, molecular networking and in silico analysis reveal bioactive antiplasmodial fractions from Aloe rigens
items.abstract: Aloe rigens Reynolds Bally (Asphodelaceae) is widely used in traditional medicine against malaria and demonstrated potent biological activity in our previous study. Despite its traditional use, its specific chemical and biological properties have not yet been comprehensively investigated. This study aimed to identify the phytochemical constituents responsible for the antiplasmodial activity of this plant through an integrated bioguided fractionation, untargeted metabolomics, and computational approach. Bioguided fractionation of Aloe rigens leaf extracts was conducted against Plasmodium falciparum (FcB-1 strain) using the SYBR Green fluorescence assay. The bioactive dichloromethane (RD) and ethyl acetate (RE) sub-extracts were profiled by LC-HRMS/MS and GC-MS. Untargeted metabolomic analysis, combining molecular networking (GNPS) with multivariate statistical analyses (PCA and hierarchical cluster analysis, HCA), was applied to characterize the fractions and identify discriminant features associated with antiplasmodial activity. Cytotoxicity was evaluated on AB943 human fibroblast cells using a resazurin-based assay. Additionally, an in silico molecular docking study was performed to assess the binding affinity of the highlighted compounds within the receptor pocket of Plasmodium falciparum Apical Membrane Antigen 1 (PfAMA1) in complex with the invasion-inhibitory peptide R1 (PDB ID: 3SRJ). 2 Bioguided fractionation of the RE sub-extract yielded fraction F2 as the most potent antiplasmodial fraction, with an IC50 of 1.38 ± 0.48 µg/mL and a selectivity index greater than 36.2. Metabolomic profiling and multivariate statistical analyses discriminated F2 from less active fractions and highlighted its distinctive chemical signature. Three major compounds preidentified in F2 namely genistein-like (C8), 7-hydroxy-3,5 dimethylisochromen-1-one-like (C3), and eupatorin-like (C5), exhibited promising in silico binding affinities within the PfAMA1 receptor pocket, with favorable interaction profiles compared to the reference inhibitory peptide R1. This study demonstrates that integrating bioguided fractionation, untargeted metabolomics, and computational approaches is a robust strategy for accelerated identification of bioactive scaffolds from medicinal plants. The findings validate the ethnopharmacological use of Aloe rigens against malaria and highlight genistein-like, 7-hydroxy-3,5-dimethylisochromen-1-onelike, and eupatorin derivatives as promising candidates for further antimalarial drug development.
items.authors: Abdirahman Elmi, A. Said Mohamed, Kevin Calabro, Dominique Laurain-Mattar, Fatouma M. Abdoul Latif, Philippe Grellier

items.title: Micro-computed-tomography-guided multiphysics simulation: insights into enclosed microelectrochemical flow cells
items.abstract: Quantitative interpretation of hydrodynamic electrochemical measurements commonly relies on analytical models that assume idealized device geometries. However, verifying the internal geometry of fully enclosed, single-step-3D-printed electrochemical flow cells is challenging because the devices cannot be taken apart without being destroyed. Herein, X-ray micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) is used to non-destructively characterize 3D channel architectures with sub-10 µm voxel resolution. The 3D-printed channels deviate substantially from the as-designed rectangular geometry, showing corrugated sloping sidewalls and a sagging, undulating ceiling. Yet, employing true (micro-CT-generated) geometries in three-dimensional multiphysics models of fluid flow and mass transport yielded currents in agreement with the channel flow electrode limiting current equation (based on flux equations formalized by Levich) for rectangular channels! This agreement and analysis of transport demonstrate that sidewall corrugation/slope and ceiling sag/undulation do not account for experimental deviations from ideal hydrodynamic behavior. Yet both the simulated and theory results deviate by 30-40% from experimental voltammetry, indicating a discrepancy that geometric non-idealities do not explain. Together, this suggests the disagreement between theory and experiment arises from incomplete consumption of the redox probe at the electrode surface, a condition consistent with the 3D-printed composite electrodes being partially blocked. More broadly, the work establishes the combination of micro-CT, multiphysics simulation, and experiment as a general, non-destructive framework for characterizing complex hydrodynamic electrochemical systems.
items.authors: Mostafa Mahmoudi, Cameron Darvish, Edgar M. Manriquez, Glen D. O’Neil, Martin Andrew Edwards

items.title: ARMS: an Automated Robotized human-Mimicking Solid sampling system
items.abstract: Chemists sample solid materials such as powders, highly viscous fluids, and semi-solids with a spatula in labs every day. Yet, this action remains the key bottleneck in the development of fully automated chemistry laboratories. While a handful of specialist tools have been developed to autonomously manipulate solids, these approaches target a limited range of material properties. In this work, we approach the problem from the other perspective by studying the capabilities of chemists to gain insights into the design of a generalist solid sampling approach with the aim of spanning the entire range of possible material properties. We observed and demonstrated that the key capabilities are characterizing, identifying the material descriptors that map material properties to actions; scooping, adding material to the spatula; depositing, removing material from the spatula; weighing, measuring the mass transferred; and auxiliary actions such as cleaning the spatula. We demonstrate how each of these actions can be combined in a bimanual robot platform and sample seven of nine materials chosen to span the range of possible materials. In order to achieve this performance, we leverage low-data learning from demonstration techniques such that demonstration collection takes less than an hour and training lasts less than a minute, exploit geometric structure, and transfer to novel materials within a descriptor class. Notably, we were able to move not only simpler granular free-flowing materials such as NaCl but also sticky materials such as honey, reaching standard deviations of 1.5–3.3 mg and 2.8–10.1 mg with scoop depth predicting delivered mass at 0.70 R2 0.93 and 0.28 R2 0.66, respectively.
items.authors: Jasper Tan, James Hermus, Emmanuel Senft, Sylvain Calinon, Pascal Miéville

items.title: Machine-learning force-field scoring rivals free-energy perturbation for congeneric ligand ranking across public benchmarks
items.abstract: Relative binding free-energy (RBFE) methods such as free-energy perturbation (FEP) set the accuracy standard for ranking congeneric ligands in structure-based drug design, but their computational cost limits throughput. Machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) now approach quantum-chemical accuracy at a small fraction of that cost, raising the question of whether they can recover much of RBFE’s ranking accuracy while remaining computationally efficient. We introduce a static-score methodology called taqo and benchmark 10 MLFF variants spanning 6 model families (UMA, MACE, Orb, eSEN, AIMNet2, AllScAIP), together with a classical molecular-mechanics force field, on a uniform static-pocket protocol, correlated against experiment across 22 benchmark systems. We find that the ten MLFFs cannot be resolved from one another at this sample size, while every one of them significantly outranks the classical force field reference, at a few seconds per ligand on a single GPU. Against published OpenFE and FEP+ results on the same systems and the same ligand sets, taqo is statistically indistinguishable from OpenFE and significantly below FEP+, at roughly three orders of magnitude lower cost. On the congeneric JACS subset taqo and FEP+ are statistically indistinguishable. On the same benchmark poses taqo outperforms classical docking scores and is statistically indistinguishable from deep-learning affinity models, without any affinity-specific training. Together these establish MLFF interaction-energy scoring as a practical high-throughput approach for lead optimization.
items.authors: Kevin Ryczko, Sarah Maier, Amogh Sood, Patrick Rowe, Harish Ramadas, Lorenzo Boninsegna

items.title: Economics-inspired molecular reactivity descriptors from atom-resolved reactivity inequality
items.abstract: Reactivity descriptors in conceptual density functional theory (DFT) usually belong to one of two broad families. Global descriptors give one value per molecule, which is easy to compare between molecules but says nothing about which parts of the molecule are more reactive. Local descriptors show how reactivity varies within a molecule and point to its most reactive atoms, but their dimension changes from one molecule to the next, which makes them hard to compare. Mapping global reactivity onto atoms is well established; the reverse, compressing a local reactivity map into a few informative numbers, is not. Economics has long faced the equivalent problem of summarising how wealth is shared across a population. Here we borrow its solution, the Gini coefficient, and apply it to the atom-condensed dual descriptor. The positive and negative parts of the dual descriptor give two Gini reactivity descriptors, Gp and Gn, that measure how unevenly the response to nucleophilic and to electrophilic attack is spread across a molecule. Tested on three controlled series of substituted carbonyls, conjugated ketones and conjugated amines, Gp and Gn behave as chemically sensible measures. They separate inductive from conjugative perturbations, respond differently to electronwithdrawing and electron-donating groups, and trace a shift from localised to delocalised response as conjugation grows. The two descriptors carry distinct mechanistic information and are promising compact features for data-driven chemistry. More broadly, this work shows that tools developed to measure inequality in societies can quantify how reactivity is shared within a molecule, and that crossing disciplinary boundaries can open new ways of reading electronic structure.
items.authors: Surya Darshan Pai, Isaac Vidal-Daza, Frank De Proft, Francisco J. Martin-Martinez

items.title: A Roadmap for Supercrystallography: From Single-Supercrystal Diffraction to the Atomic Structure of Colloidal Nanocrystals
items.abstract: Colloidal nanocrystals are complex objects, comprising a solid inorganic core and a soft shell of organic ligands, both of which contribute to defining their properties. Obtaining an atomically precise description of both components remains an open challenge. Yet, these hybrid building blocks can self-assemble into supercrystals sufficiently large to be isolated and analyzed individually. It may therefore come as a surprise that single-supercrystal X-ray diffraction is not routinely used to investigate the structure of their constituent nanocrystals. Here, we propose a roadmap for establishing supercrystallography as the science of obtaining structural information about colloidal building blocks through diffraction experiments performed on their supercrystals. We review existing examples of single-supercrystal X-ray diffraction, examine the opportunities that may emerge from extending crystallographic methods to colloidal supercrystals, and discuss the main challenges that must be overcome to realize this vision. Drawing inspiration from the crystallography of nanoclusters and proteins, systems that share deep similarities with colloidal nanocrystals, we outline a possible path connecting state-of-the-art experiments to complete atomistic models through innovative data-analysis strategies. Finally, we consider how supercrystallography could complement existing characterization techniques, and develop into an accessible framework for investigating the structure of colloidal nanocrystals and their surface chemistry.
items.authors: Stefano Toso, Dmitry Baranov, William A. Tisdale

items.title: Proton Solvation Thermochemistry: A Temperature-Resolved Calibration from Ammonium Acids
items.abstract: Chemical reactions involving protonation are ubiquitous in nature, yet their accurate description using static quantum-chemical methods remains challenging. Here, we derive a temperature-resolved aqueous free energy of H+ (G◦,aq H+ ) by combining experimental pKa data for 12 ammonium acids over 293–333 K with a high-level composite quantum-chemical protocol based on LNO-CCSD(T)/CBS energies, CPCM solvation, and conformational thermochemistry. Thermodynamic analysis gives G◦,aq H+ = −270.0 kcal/mol at 298 K, within 0.3 kcal/mol of the canonical literature value (Tissandier et al., 1998). The fitted parameters are robust under cross-validation, and validation on an independent set of 18 acids yields a mean absolute error of 0.70 pKa units.
items.authors: Khaled Jaradat, Bence Balázs Mészáros, János Daru

items.title: Phase-field modeling of porosity formation and evolution during hydrogen-based iron oxide reduction
items.abstract: Hydrogen-based direct reduction of iron oxides (HyDRI) offers a low-emission route to solid-state ironmaking by replacing carbon-based reductants with hydrogen. The mass loss associated with oxygen removal generates porosity. The evolving pore network influences reduction kinetics through changes in transport pathways and internal reaction surfaces. Here, we develop a phase-field framework that couples solid-state oxygen transport, the wüstite–ferrite transformation, and pore evolution during the rate-controlling step of HyDRI. Pore generation follows the local transformation rate at the advancing reaction front, whereas surface diffusion redistributes existing porosity. The newly formed solid–pore interfaces provide additional oxygen-removal sites, coupling pore evolution back to front propagation. The simulations show that increasing reduction-generated porosity drives a transition from isolated pores to connected channels, raising the fraction of pore space connected to the external surface from approximately 7% to 97%. Additional internal reaction surfaces shorten the time to 90% reduction by approximately 15%, demonstrating how pore formation accelerates further reduction. Faster front propagation preserves fine, tortuous pores, whereas faster surface diffusion promotes smoothing and coarsening. The resulting structures differ by more than a factor of two in the solid–pore interfacial length available for oxygen removal, even at the same reduction-generated porosity. Pore connectivity and the internal surface available for reaction therefore depend on reduction history and cannot be inferred from porosity alone. These findings provide a physical basis for linking local pore evolution to gas access and overall reduction kinetics at larger scales.
items.authors: Kartik Sunil Umate, Yang Bai, Bob Svendsen, Dierk Raabe

items.title: Direct generation of a prototypical n-pentyl peroxy radical reveals how mixedfate chemical regimes shape product distributions
items.abstract: Organic peroxy radicals (RO2) are key branch points in atmospheric oxidation with competing fates in the troposphere: reaction with NO, reaction with HO2, self-/cross-reaction with another RO2, and isomerization. RO2 often react in mixed-fate regimes, yielding product distributions with a complex dependence on reactivity conditions. In traditional environmental chamber experiments, not all RO2 fates are equally accessible, and chemical regimes favoring RO2 self-/cross-reactions and isomerizations are poorly characterized. Here, we access these conditions in an environmental chamber via 1-iodopentane photolysis, monitoring product distributions with NH4 + chemical ionization mass spectrometry. We tune the relative importance of these reaction pathways by varying the initial conditions, spanning bimolecular lifetimes from ~100-2000 s. Across conditions, the major observed C5 product, C5H10O3 (~40-60% yield), requires at least one RO2 isomerization to form, demonstrating the importance of downstream RO2 unimolecular reactions even if they are not the major fate of upstream RO2. Model mechanisms partially reproduce observed product distributions but cannot quantitatively capture variations with changing RO2 fate. Discrepancies suggest poorly-understood RO2 cross-reactions substantially influence product distributions. Conditions favoring RO2 isomerization unintuitively enhance both fragmentation and accretion via downstream functionalized alkoxy and peroxy radical chemistry. Results illuminate important gaps in existing atmospheric reaction mechanisms when predicting product distributions in mixed-fate chemical regimes.
items.authors: Cooper K. Crabtree, Sara E. Murphy, Victoria P. Barber

items.title: Conductive Polymer Binder for Long-Term Stability of GaN Anode at Elevated Temperatures
items.abstract: Temperature is a major factor influencing battery cycle life, with elevated temperatures generally accelerating capacity degradation. Here, we employed poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS), a conductive polymer, as a binder to stabilize GaN anodes for long-term cycling at 55°C. The GaN anode with the PEDOT:PSS binder (GaN/PE) exhibits over a 40× increase in its electrical conductivity compared to the GaN anode with a conventional polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder (GaN/PVDF). The GaN/PE anode achieves a specific capacity of up to 855.3 mAh/g at 0.1 A/g, approaching the theoretical capacity of GaN (960 mAh/g) and approximately tripling the maximum capacity of the GaN/PVDF anode under the same operating conditions. In addition, the GaN/PE anode demonstrates long-term stability, retaining about 600 mAh/g after 500 cycles at 55 °C, while the GaN/PVDF anode achieves only half of that value after 500 cycles. Notably, previous reports on Si-based anodes operated within 45-70°C show a dramatic decrease in their capacity, remaining about 600 mAh/g after only 100 cycles. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations explain the long-term stability of the GaN/PE anodes through improved thermomechanical stability of PEDOT:PSS, with a thermal expansion coefficient less than half that of PVDF, suggesting the reduction of thermal expansion mismatch within the GaN/PE anode during high-temperature operation. Operando X-ray diffraction exhibits crystalline stability in the GaN/PE anode, with less crystalline degradation than the GaN/PVDF anode. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) further demonstrates the stability of the GaN/PE anode, showing a 10-ohm decrease in charge-transfer resistance (Rct) after 500 cycles, whereas the GaN/PVDF anode shows an over 10× increase in Rct. . Together, our study proposes a binder technology approach that stabilizes GaN anodes by mitigating thermal degradation, enabling long-term cycling stability in LIBs for high-temperature applications.
items.authors: Thuy Thi Bich Tran, Nicholas P. Hattrup, John S. Okasinski, Renuka Hyderkhan, Gerald J. Wang, B. Reeja Jayan

items.title: Oxidative ArylSF4-tetrafluoroethylation to N-hydroxydicarboximides via in situ generated Silver intermediate from silver(I) fluoride.
items.abstract: An efficient and streamlined protocol for the ArylSF4-tetrafluoroethylation of N-hydroxyimides has been developed utilizing an in situ generated silver- (1,2,2,2-tetrafluoro-1-(SF4Aryl)ethyl reagent. While traditional methods rely heavily on common fluoroalkylating agents, Aryl-SF4 containing polyfluoroalkylating reagents remain very rare. Herein, we generating a highly reactive silver-tetrafluoroethyl(SF4Aryl) species in situ, followed by its immediate oxidative radical reaction with a diverse range of N-hydroxyimides. Under optimized reaction conditions, using N-Bromosuccinimide as the terminal oxidant, the corresponding Aryl-SF4 containing tetrafluoroethylated products were obtained in moderate to good yields (up to 69 %). This transition-metal-promoted tandem process exhibits broad substrate scope, high functional group tolerance, and eliminates the need for the isolation of unstable organometallic intermediates. Given the high demand for fluorinated motifs in medicinal chemistry and materials science, this operational simplicity offers a powerful, robust strategy for late-stage SF4 containing polyfluoroalkylation.
items.authors: Ratnakar Reddy Kuchukulla, Norio Shibata

items.title: Electronic Structure of Cobalamins Defined by High Energy Resolution Fluorescence Detected X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy: Insights into Photochemical Axial Bond Cleavage in the CarH Photoreceptor
items.abstract: Nature utilizes cobalamin photochemistry within photoreceptor proteins to regulate vital biological functions. Rationalization of structure-function relationships that selectively activate/deactivate cobalamin photochemistry is essential for understanding how organisms leverage this photosensitivity. In this work, we systematically investigated the electronic structure and photochemistry of four cobalamin variants—both free in solution and bound to the CarH photoreceptor protein—using Cobalt Kα1 high-energy-resolution fluorescence-detected X-ray absorption near-edge structure (HERFD-XANES) spectroscopy and (time-dependent) density functional theory ((TD-)DFT) calculations. Stark differences in HERFD-XANES spectra between alkyl- and non-alkyl cobalamins are observed, with the former exhibiting more intense pre-edge features. TD-DFT simulations reproduce the observed pre-edge intensity trends and show that increased intensity correlates with enhanced cobalt 3dz 2/4pz mixing arising from greater axialligand σ-donor covalency. The higher resolution afforded by HERFD also enables identification of 1s → corrin π* pre-edge satellites that are obscured in lower-resolution measurements. Analysis of these features indicates that their intensity provides evidence for the presence of cobalt 4pz/3dz 2 orbital character in molecular corrin π* orbitals. This finding supports a mechanism for alkylcobalamin photochemistry and Co–C bond cleavage in which photoexcitation into a corrin π* orbital is followed by donation into the cobalt 3dz 2 orbital. Interestingly, HERFD-XANES profiles between free and CarH-bound cobalamins are similar, demonstrating that the cofactor’s groundstate electronic structure is largely preserved when protein-bound. This indicates that CarH tunes AdoCbl photochemistry in the photoexcited state. Finally, we demonstrate that a truncated CarH variant that permits higher Co concentrations yields high-quality HERFD-XANES with strong sensitivity to geometric and electronic structure, suggesting that applying this technique in future time-resolved pump-probe investigations could lead to breakthroughs in elucidating the transient intermediates that drive CarH photoactivity.
items.authors: Emma Wall, Zhibo Qi, Shusaku Hayama, Michael L. Baker, Sam Hay

items.title: Charge Loss of Proteins in vacuo: Implications for Native Mass Spectrometry and Ion Mobility
items.abstract: Native ion mobility–mass spectrometry (IM-MS) is a powerful biophysical technique for characterizing protein structure. Because individual charge states often exhibit distinct structural dynamics, accurate IM-MS measurements require charge states to be examined independently. Although anecdotal reports among mass spectrometrists suggest that protein ions can lose charges during native IM-MS experiments, a thorough investigation of this phenomenon has been lacking. Here, we demonstrate that protein ions undergo charge loss inside the mass spectrometer as a direct consequence of gas-phase collisions, potentially leading to altered charge state distributions and ion mobility data. This effect was consistently observed across two instrument platforms (Synapt G2-S and Q Exactive UHMR), both ion polarities (positive and negative mode) and for three proteins (bovine serum albumin, myoglobin, and immunoglobulin G). Systematic investigations of instrumental parameters revealed that collision gas pressure has the strongest impact on the magnitude of charge loss, and that higher charge states are more affected than lower charge states. We further show that this process is largely driven by the dissociation of salt adducts and can hence be minimized through desalting in solution or inside the mass spectrometer, prior to the first m/z -analyzer (usually a quadrupole). For collision-induced unfolding experiments, significant differences were found between fingerprints acquired with and without quadrupole selection, although it remains unclear whether this phenomenon is directly related to charge loss. Taken together, our study provides fundamental insights into collision-induced charge loss as a source of error in native IM-MS measurements and discusses the relevance of quadrupole m/z -selection for improving confidence in IM studies.
items.authors: Mathew Bejoy, Nicklas Österlund, Jacob S. Jordan, Kevin Pagel, Niklas Geue

items.title: Translation-rotation internal coordinates with splicing (TRICS): A new approach to molecular geometry interpolation
items.abstract: We present TRICS (Translation-Rotation Internal Coordinates with Splicing), a novel internal-coordinate-based interpolation method for generating high-quality approximations to minimum energy pathways (MEPs). Non-redundant internal coordinate (IC) systems can be used to generate chemically reasonable interpolated pathways between reactant and product structures, but it may fail for regions of configuration space where the IC system becomes numerically ill-defined. TRICS overcomes this limitation using multiple IC systems to generate separate interpolated paths that are iteratively spliced together into one continuous trajectory. We benchmarked the new method on 679 chemically diverse reactions, demonstrating excellent performance in generating interpolated pathways close to optimized transition-state structures. We further demonstrate the utility of TRICS for generating smooth and barrier-free interpolated pathways between critical points on excited-state potential energy surfaces. TRICS is available from the open-source geomeTRIC package.
items.authors: Heejune Park, Chenchen Song, Lee-Ping Wang

items.title: Photoactivated Hydrocarbon Oxidation Coupled with Ozone Decomposition with MnO2 Catalyst
items.abstract: Treatment of hydrocarbon emissions such as methane and formaldehyde require effective conversion alongside control of energy consumption and secondary pollutant formation. A continuous-flow methane and formaldehyde treatment system combining ultraviolet-C (UVC) irradiation, manganese dioxide (MnO2), and water addition was investigated in this study. Optical, thermal, and structural characterisation established the experimental platform, while irradiation on-off measurements, gas chromatography (GC), and infrared (IR) spectroscopy assessed reaction conversion, reactor response, and any residual ozone formation. Humid condition with MnO2 catalyst provides the highest methane conversion and the presence of the MnO2 suppressed ozone of the exit stream. Methane-free control experiments showed that oxygen concentration and MnO2 loading influenced the levels of ozone of the exit stream. Under humid conditions, 1.5 g of MnO2 achieved complete methane conversion across inlet concentrations of 200-10,000 ppm at an incident irradiance of 42 mW cm-2. Mixed feed experiments further demonstrated simultaneous conversion of methane, methanol, and formaldehyde with conversions at 100%, 87% and 86%, respectively under an incident irradiance of 85 mW cm-2. These results established the lab-scale potential of UV-MnO2 treatment for methane and volatile organic compounds.
items.authors: Zhengyi Wu, Ning Wang, Tze Yeung Cho, Tzia Ming Onn

items.title: Rare Earth Elements Recovery with Membranes, Additive Manufacturing, and AI/ML Workflows
items.abstract: Rare earth element (REE) extraction and separation from secondary sources are entering a critical stage as the demand for REE-enabled materials accelerates while conventional supply chains face technical, economic, and environmental pressure. Although significant progress has been made in REE separations from primary resources, inherent variability of secondary sources introduces substantial chemical and processing challenges, rendering REEs an ever-moving target for extraction and production. In this review, we discuss conventional and novel methods in separations, additive manufacturing–enabled separations, role of AI in separations, data driven approaches, AI/ML implementation, self-driving labs, and AI/ML workflows.
items.authors: Pasindu Samaraweera, Ilia N. Ivanov, M. Parans Paranthaman, Rigoberto Advincula

items.title: From sequences and structures to fitness, folding and function: challenges in the age of AI
items.abstract: Deep-learning models have transformed our ability to predict the phenotypic effects of sequence perturbations. Protein language models (pLMs) score the evolutionary propensity of any amino-acid substitution, emerging as fast and accurate predictors of fitness changes. Inverse-folding (IF) models add structural information and are powerful alternatives for estimating folding-stability changes. But these likelihoods are imperfect and sometimes biased predictors of the biological quantities they are used to measure. Scaling pLMs has shown that bigger models do not always outperform smaller ones. IF models sometimes read sequence conservation as a stability constraint, which leads to biases when this signal is used to isolate functional contributions beyond folding. We review here the strategies emerging to mitigate, and where possible overcome, these limitations. Highlights:- Scaling protein language models does not close the likelihood–fitness gap - Inverse-folding models can read functional conservation as lost stability - Disentangling function from stability inherits both biases - Emerging strategies are attempting to address these issues
items.authors: Ezequiel A. Galpern, Charles W. J. Pugh, Mafalda Dias, Jonathan Frazer

items.title: Battery models as controlled laboratory methods: simulated results across the operating envelope, code verification and a physics-informed surrogate
items.abstract: Laboratories increasingly base formulation, protocol and safety decisions on battery models, yet models rarely receive the controls that laboratory methods do: versions, validation on unseen data, reproducible records and verification of the numerical solution. We report a suite of 9 registered models that run inside a laboratory platform (a cell simulator with equivalent-circuit, single-particle, electrolyte-corrected and transient-electrolyte rungs, electrode balancing, pulse and impedance predictors, a plating-limited charging optimiser, a receding-horizon charge controller, an unscented Kalman filter with a stability review, and a mechanistic ageing model), together with the results they produce for a published cell parameterisation and the evidence for trusting those results. Half-way through a 1C discharge, solid diffusion, electrolyte transport and contact resistance cost 85, 49 and 50 mV; the electrolyte-corrected and transient-electrolyte rungs agree within 25 mV at 1C but diverge by 1,051 mV at 3C, where the latter depletes its electrolyte.
